correctness.rationale: For theta lengths a,b,c≥2, every spanning tree deletes one edge from each of two different paths, giving W=ab+ac+bc equiprobable trees. Explicit deleted-edge marginals and joint probabilities give a strictly negative kernel for every pair of distinct deleted edges. Covariance of vertex degrees sums that kernel over incident-edge pairs, yielding strict negativity on all nonedges and two rational adjacent-edge expressions. Expanding the pole-adjacent numerator at r=2 into x²y+xy²+8xy+4x+4y establishes its only zero at (2,2,2); the internal-adjacent numerator has its only zero at (3,2,2). Independent exact enumeration checked 216 path triples and 35865 assertions, including covariance row sums. The proof covers all integer lengths, not only finite computations.

originality.rationale: The evaluated claim is the uniform sign equivalence between labeled host adjacency and degree covariance across every theta-path length triple, with an exact exceptional-zero classification. Cherkashin–Petrov–Prozorov (2022) classify real stability rather than signed covariances. Fita Sanmartín–Schnörr–Hamprecht (2024) obtain general graphwise covariance formulas, but do not derive the global theta sign inequalities or adjacency reconstruction. Rapoport (2025) gives a general degree-field law without the evaluated theta specialization. Searches of related literature and mathematical result records did not locate a dominating qualitative sign theorem; implicit older specialization remains a risk.

value.rationale: The three-path theta family is the canonical simple two-terminal bicyclic graph. Its full labeled adjacency can be recovered from the second-order fluctuations of one natural stochastic object—uniform spanning-tree vertex degrees—without higher moments or a matrix inverse. The universal sign test, unexpected nonnegative adjacent versus strictly negative nonadjacent dichotomy, and exactly classified small zero boundaries are natural structural facts relevant to graph identification and dependence measures. This property holds even for longer theta graphs whose degree-enumerator polynomial is not real stable, distinguishing pairwise sign structure from polynomial stability. The theorem is not merely a numerical covariance computation.
